previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, chronic pain, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted after being found down and reporting a possible assault. He presented with alcohol intoxication and signs of withdrawal, including tremors, diaphoresis, and nausea. Trauma imaging showed no acute fractures or intracranial hemorrhage, though head CTs were limited by motion. He refused a repeat head CT due to radiation concerns. Treatment focused on alcohol withdrawal management with scheduled diazepam, IV fluids for volume depletion, and vitamin supplementation. His mental status improved, and withdrawal symptoms stabilized. Despite medical advice, he chose to leave against medical advice on the third day, declining further detoxification or rehab referral. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up and continue care.
